Use technologies with a presence on endpoints to detect cyber health issues (e.g., missing patches, malware infections, unauthorized software), and redirect the endpoints to a remediation environment before access is authorized

categories.name: Adverse Event Analysis
categories.description: Anomalies, indicators of compromise, and other potentially adverse events are analyzed to characterize the events and detect cybersecurity incidents.

subcategories.description: Potentially adverse events are analyzed to better understand associated activities
subcategories.guidance: Analyze detected alerts and anomalies to determine attack techniques, tactics, and procedures (TTPs). Classify events by type and severity. Enrich event data with asset information, user context, and threat intelligence. Distinguish false positives from true threats. Document analysis findings and use them to improve detection capabilities.
implementation_examples: Use security information and event management (SIEM) or other tools to continuously monitor log events for known malicious and suspicious activity
Utilize up-to-date cyber threat intelligence in log analysis tools to improve detection accuracy and characterize threat actors, their methods, and indicators of compromise
Regularly conduct manual reviews of log events for technologies that cannot be sufficiently monitored through automation
Use log analysis tools to generate reports on their findings

subcategories.description: Information is correlated from multiple sources
subcategories.guidance: Correlate events and alerts from multiple monitoring sources (network, endpoint, identity, application, cloud) to identify broader attack patterns that individual alerts may not reveal. Use SIEM or extended detection and response (XDR) platforms for correlation. Define correlation rules based on known attack patterns and tactics. Update correlation logic as new threats emerge.
implementation_examples: Constantly transfer log data generated by other sources to a relatively small number of log servers
Use event correlation technology (e.g., SIEM) to collect information captured by multiple sources
Utilize cyber threat intelligence to help correlate events among log sources

subcategories.description: The estimated impact and scope of adverse events are understood
subcategories.guidance: When analyzing adverse events, assess the potential impact and scope including affected systems, data that may be exposed or compromised, operational disruption, and mission impact. Update scope estimates as the investigation progresses and more information becomes available. Use impact assessments to prioritize response actions and resource allocation.
implementation_examples: Use SIEMs or other tools to estimate impact and scope, and review and refine the estimates
A person creates their own estimates of impact and scope

subcategories.description: Information on adverse events is provided to authorized staff and tools
subcategories.guidance: Distribute relevant event information and alerts to authorized security personnel and automated response tools in a timely manner. Define escalation paths based on event severity. Provide context-enriched alerts to analysts. Integrate detection tools with incident response systems to enable rapid response. Ensure notification reaches the right people without alert fatigue.
implementation_examples: Use cybersecurity software to generate alerts and provide them to the security operations center (SOC), incident responders, and incident response tools
Incident responders and other authorized personnel can access log analysis findings at all times
Automatically create and assign tickets in the organization’s ticketing system when certain types of alerts occur
Manually create and assign tickets in the organization’s ticketing system when technical staff discover indicators of compromise

subcategories.description: Cyber threat intelligence and other contextual information are integrated into the analysis
subcategories.guidance: Enrich security event analysis with cyber threat intelligence including indicators of compromise (IOCs), threat actor TTPs, and vulnerability information. Integrate threat intelligence feeds into detection platforms. Use intelligence to contextualize alerts and prioritize analysis. Contribute relevant threat intelligence back to sharing communities.
implementation_examples: Securely provide cyber threat intelligence feeds to detection technologies, processes, and personnel
Securely provide information from asset inventories to detection technologies, processes, and personnel
Rapidly acquire and analyze vulnerability disclosures for the organization’s technologies from suppliers, vendors, and third-party security advisories

subcategories.description: Incidents are declared when adverse events meet the defined incident criteria
subcategories.guidance: Define clear criteria for declaring cybersecurity incidents based on event type, severity, and potential impact. Train analysts on applying incident criteria consistently. When criteria are met, trigger the formal incident response process without delay. Document the declaration decision including the basis for it. Avoid both under-reporting (missing true incidents) and over-reporting (alert fatigue).
implementation_examples: Apply incident criteria to known and assumed characteristics of activity in order to determine whether an incident should be declared
Take known false positives into account when applying incident criteria

functions.name: RESPOND
functions.description: Actions regarding a detected cybersecurity incident are taken.

categories.name: Incident Management
categories.description: Responses to detected cybersecurity incidents are managed.

subcategories.description: The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared
subcategories.guidance: Execute the documented incident response plan upon incident declaration. Activate the incident response team and assign roles. Coordinate with relevant third parties including managed security service providers, legal counsel, law enforcement, and affected suppliers. Document all actions taken during response. Maintain command and communication throughout the incident.
implementation_examples: Detection technologies automatically report confirmed incidents
Request incident response assistance from the organization’s incident response outsourcer
Designate an incident lead for each incident
Initiate execution of additional cybersecurity plans as needed to support incident response (for example, business continuity and disaster recovery)

subcategories.description: Incident reports are triaged and validated
subcategories.guidance: Establish a triage process for incoming incident reports and alerts. Validate reported events to confirm they meet incident criteria. Assess severity and priority. Assign incidents to appropriate response teams based on type and severity. Document triage decisions and rationale.
implementation_examples: Preliminarily review incident reports to confirm that they are cybersecurity-related and necessitate incident response activities
Apply criteria to estimate the severity of an incident

subcategories.description: Incidents are categorized and prioritized
subcategories.guidance: Categorize confirmed incidents by type (e.g., ransomware, data breach, denial of service, insider threat, phishing). Prioritize incidents based on severity, mission impact, data sensitivity, and regulatory notification requirements. Use prioritization to guide resource allocation and escalation decisions.
implementation_examples: Further review and categorize incidents based on the type of incident (e.g., data breach, ransomware, DDoS, account compromise)
Prioritize incidents based on their scope, likely impact, and time-critical nature
Select incident response strategies for active incidents by balancing the need to quickly recover from an incident with the need to observe the attacker or conduct a more thorough investigation

subcategories.description: Incidents are escalated or elevated as needed
subcategories.guidance: Define escalation criteria and paths for incidents requiring senior leadership involvement, legal notification, law enforcement engagement, or external expert assistance. Escalate promptly when criteria are met. Provide escalation recipients with clear situational information. Adjust response resources based on escalation decisions.
implementation_examples: Track and validate the status of all ongoing incidents
Coordinate incident escalation or elevation with designated internal and external stakeholders

subcategories.description: The criteria for initiating incident recovery are applied
subcategories.guidance: Define clear criteria for determining when it is safe and appropriate to begin recovery operations, such as eradication of the threat, removal of attacker persistence, and patching of exploited vulnerabilities. Apply these criteria before initiating recovery to avoid re-compromise. Document the criteria check and the decision to begin recovery.
implementation_examples: Apply incident recovery criteria to known and assumed characteristics of the incident to determine whether incident recovery processes should be initiated
Take the possible operational disruption of incident recovery activities into account

categories.name: Incident Analysis
categories.description: Investigations are conducted to ensure effective response and support forensics and recovery activities.

subcategories.description: Analysis is performed to establish what has taken place during an incident and the root cause of the incident
subcategories.guidance: Conduct thorough forensic analysis to determine the timeline of the incident, attack vectors used, systems and data affected, and root cause. Use forensic tools and techniques appropriate to the environment. Document analysis findings in a structured incident report. Identify contributing factors and control failures that enabled the incident.
implementation_examples: Determine the sequence of events that occurred during the incident and which assets and resources were involved in each event
Attempt to determine what vulnerabilities, threats, and threat actors were directly or indirectly involved in the incident
Analyze the incident to find the underlying, systemic root causes
Check any cyber deception technology for additional information on attacker behavior

subcategories.description: Actions performed during an investigation are recorded, and the records' integrity and provenance are preserved
subcategories.guidance: Maintain detailed and contemporaneous records of all actions taken during the investigation including commands run, files accessed, evidence collected, and decisions made. Protect the integrity of investigation records through access controls and tamper-evident logging. Preserve chain of custody for evidence that may be used in legal proceedings.
implementation_examples: Require each incident responder and others (e.g., system administrators, cybersecurity engineers) who perform incident response tasks to record their actions and make the record immutable
Require the incident lead to document the incident in detail and be responsible for preserving the integrity of the documentation and the sources of all information being reported

subcategories.description: Incident data and metadata are collected, and their integrity and provenance are preserved
subcategories.guidance: Collect and preserve incident artifacts including system logs, network captures, memory dumps, disk images, and malware samples. Verify integrity of collected data using cryptographic hashing. Document the provenance of evidence including collection time, collector identity, and chain of custody. Store evidence securely with access controls.
implementation_examples: Collect, preserve, and safeguard the integrity of all pertinent incident data and metadata (e.g., data source, date/time of collection) based on evidence preservation and chain-of-custody procedures

subcategories.description: An incident's magnitude is estimated and validated
subcategories.guidance: Estimate the full scope and magnitude of the incident including the number and types of systems affected, volume and sensitivity of data exposed, duration of unauthorized access, and business impact. Validate initial estimates as investigation progresses and refine as new evidence is discovered. Use magnitude assessments to guide notification decisions and recovery prioritization.
implementation_examples: Review other potential targets of the incident to search for indicators of compromise and evidence of persistence
Automatically run tools on targets to look for indicators of compromise and evidence of persistence

categories.name: Incident Response Reporting and Communication
categories.description: Response activities are coordinated with internal and external stakeholders as required by laws, regulations, or policies.

subcategories.description: Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents
subcategories.guidance: Notify internal stakeholders (executive leadership, legal, communications, HR, affected business units) and external stakeholders (regulators, affected customers and individuals, law enforcement, cyber insurers) of incidents according to legal, regulatory, and contractual notification timelines. Prepare accurate and clear notifications tailored to each audience. Track notification obligations and document notifications sent.
implementation_examples: Follow the organization’s breach notification procedures after discovering a data breach incident, including notifying affected customers
Notify business partners and customers of incidents in accordance with contractual requirements
Notify law enforcement agencies and regulatory bodies of incidents based on criteria in the incident response plan and management approval

subcategories.description: Information is shared with designated internal and external stakeholders
subcategories.guidance: Share relevant incident information with internal teams and external partners such as ISACs, peer organizations, and government agencies to enable coordinated response and broader threat awareness. Follow information sharing agreements, legal restrictions, and data classification policies when sharing. Use appropriate sharing formats and marking conventions (e.g., TLP).
implementation_examples: Securely share information consistent with response plans and information sharing agreements
Voluntarily share information about an attacker’s observed TTPs, with all sensitive data removed, with an Information Sharing and Analysis Center (ISAC)
Notify HR when malicious insider activity occurs
Regularly update senior leadership on the status of major incidents
Follow the rules and protocols defined in contracts for incident information sharing between the organization and its suppliers
Coordinate crisis communication methods between the organization and its critical suppliers

categories.name: Incident Mitigation
categories.description: Activities are performed to prevent expansion of an event and mitigate its effects.

subcategories.description: Incidents are contained
subcategories.guidance: Take containment actions to limit the spread of the incident and prevent further damage. Containment actions may include isolating affected systems from the network, revoking compromised credentials, blocking malicious network traffic, disabling affected accounts, and taking systems offline. Balance containment urgency against business impact. Document all containment actions taken.
implementation_examples: Cybersecurity technologies (e.g., antivirus software) and cybersecurity features of other technologies (e.g., operating systems, network infrastructure devices) automatically perform containment actions
Allow incident responders to manually select and perform containment actions
Allow a third party (e.g., internet service provider, managed security service provider) to perform containment actions on behalf of the organization
Automatically transfer compromised endpoints to a remediation virtual local area network (VLAN)

subcategories.description: Incidents are eradicated
subcategories.guidance: Remove the root cause and all traces of the incident from affected systems. Eradication actions may include removing malware, closing exploited vulnerabilities, removing attacker persistence mechanisms (backdoors, rogue accounts), and rebuilding compromised systems from known-good images. Verify eradication is complete before initiating recovery.
implementation_examples: Cybersecurity technologies and cybersecurity features of other technologies (e.g., operating systems, network infrastructure devices) automatically perform eradication actions
Allow incident responders to manually select and perform eradication actions
Allow a third party (e.g., managed security service provider) to perform eradication actions on behalf of the organization

functions.name: RECOVER
functions.description: Assets and operations affected by a cybersecurity incident are restored.

categories.name: Incident Recovery Plan Execution
categories.description: Restoration activities are performed to ensure operational availability of systems and services affected by cybersecurity incidents.

subcategories.description: The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated from the incident response process
subcategories.guidance: Execute documented recovery procedures when triggered by the incident management process. Activate recovery teams and assign responsibilities. Follow the sequence of recovery actions defined in recovery plans. Coordinate recovery activities across teams and with relevant third parties. Document actions taken and track progress against recovery objectives.
implementation_examples: Begin recovery procedures during or after incident response processes
Make all individuals with recovery responsibilities aware of the plans for recovery and the authorizations required to implement each aspect of the plans

subcategories.description: Recovery actions are selected, scoped, prioritized, and performed
subcategories.guidance: Select recovery actions appropriate to the incident type, affected systems, and recovery objectives. Scope recovery to affected systems and data. Prioritize recovery based on mission criticality and business impact — restore the most critical functions first. Execute prioritized recovery actions in a controlled and documented manner.
implementation_examples: Select recovery actions based on the criteria defined in the incident response plan and available resources
Change planned recovery actions based on a reassessment of organizational needs and resources

subcategories.description: The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before using them for restoration
subcategories.guidance: Before using backups or recovery images for restoration, verify their integrity using cryptographic checksums or hashes. Confirm backups are unaffected by the incident (e.g., not encrypted by ransomware or corrupted). Test restoration in a non-production environment where possible before applying to production. Use only verified, trusted restoration assets.
implementation_examples: Check restoration assets for indicators of compromise, file corruption, and other integrity issues before use

subcategories.description: Critical mission functions and cybersecurity risk management are considered to establish post-incident operational norms
subcategories.guidance: Consider mission requirements and ongoing cybersecurity risks when defining post-incident operating conditions. Do not restore operations until the threat is fully eradicated. Assess residual risks before resuming normal operations. Define temporary operating procedures if full restoration is not immediately possible. Obtain appropriate approval before declaring normal operations.
implementation_examples: Use business impact and system categorization records (including service delivery objectives) to validate that essential services are restored in the appropriate order
Work with system owners to confirm the successful restoration of systems and the return to normal operations
Monitor the performance of restored systems to verify the adequacy of the restoration

subcategories.description: The integrity of restored assets is verified, systems and services are restored, and normal operating status is confirmed
subcategories.guidance: After restoration, verify that systems and data are complete, accurate, and secure. Conduct security checks on restored systems including scanning for malware and verifying configurations. Confirm that services are operating normally and securely before returning them to production. Obtain stakeholder confirmation that business functions have been restored.
implementation_examples: Check restored assets for indicators of compromise and remediation of root causes of the incident before production use
Verify the correctness and adequacy of the restoration actions taken before putting a restored system online

subcategories.description: The end of incident recovery is declared based on criteria, and incident-related documentation is completed
subcategories.guidance: Define criteria for declaring the end of incident recovery such as full restoration of services, eradication verification, and completion of initial remediation. Formally declare recovery complete when criteria are met. Complete all incident documentation including timeline, impact summary, response actions taken, and lessons learned. Retain records per policy and legal requirements.
implementation_examples: Prepare an after-action report that documents the incident itself, the response and recovery actions taken, and lessons learned
Declare the end of incident recovery once the criteria are met

categories.name: Incident Recovery Communication
categories.description: Restoration activities are coordinated with internal and external parties.

subcategories.description: Recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities are communicated to designated internal and external stakeholders
subcategories.guidance: Provide regular status updates on recovery progress to internal stakeholders (leadership, operations, affected business units) and relevant external stakeholders (regulators, major customers, insurers). Define communication frequency and format based on stakeholder needs and incident severity. Document all communications made during recovery.
implementation_examples: Securely share recovery information, including restoration progress, consistent with response plans and information sharing agreements
Regularly update senior leadership on recovery status and restoration progress for major incidents
Follow the rules and protocols defined in contracts for incident information sharing between the organization and its suppliers
Coordinate crisis communication between the organization and its critical suppliers

subcategories.description: Public updates on incident recovery are shared using approved methods and messaging
subcategories.guidance: Release approved public statements about the incident and recovery progress through official communication channels (press releases, website, social media) in accordance with organizational communications policy and legal guidance. Ensure public messaging is accurate, timely, and reviewed by legal and communications teams before release. Coordinate with law enforcement and regulators before making public disclosures that may affect investigations.
implementation_examples: Follow the organization’s breach notification procedures for recovering from a data breach incident
Explain the steps being taken to recover from the incident and to prevent a recurrence
